Italics 3. Underline 4. Hyperlink 5. Headers 6. Images 7. Line breaks 8. Bullets 9. Numbered list 10. Tables 11. R Plot 12. Dynamic documents in R (with citation, footnotes and bibliography) ## Running R code chunks R Markdown are dynamic documents in which we can embed R code, for example: **Code Chunk:** ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} x <- c("YY") print(x) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` [1] "YY" ``` ::: ::: **Output:** ``` [1] "YY" ``` Note that the `echo = FALSE` parameter can be added to the code chunk to prevent printing of the R code that generated only the output. ``` {r, echo=FALSE} ``` We can also try `echo = TRUE` parameter (shown above), as well as `eval = FALSE/TRUE` and `include = FALSE/TRUE`. ## Let's look at some formatting ### 1. Bold **Code:** ```markdown This is a normal text This is a **bold** text This is a __bold__ text ``` **Output:** This is a normal text This is a **bold** text This is a __bold__ text --- ### 2. Italics **Code:** ```markdown This is a normal text This is a *italics* text This is a _italics_ text ``` **Output:** This is a normal text This is a *italics* text This is a _italics_ text --- ### 3. Underline **Code:** ```markdown underlined text ``` **Output:** underlined text --- ### 4. Hyperlinks **Code:** ```markdown Here is a [link](https://www.econ.chula.ac.th/) to CU Econ website. ``` **Output:** Here is a [link](https://www.econ.chula.ac.th/) to CU Econ website. --- ### 5. Headers **Code:** ```markdown # Header 1 ## Header 2 ### Header 3 #### Header 4 ``` **Output:** # Header 1 ## Header 2 ### Header 3 #### Header 4 --- ### 6. Images **Code:** ```markdown ![picture](./Picture.jpg){width=50%} ``` **Note:** Image will appear if Picture.jpg exists in your working directory. --- ### 7. Line breaks **Code:** ```markdown (Double space after each sentence will move the next sentence to the next line) Or jump a line Like this ^^ ``` --- ### 8. Bullets **Code:** ```markdown * This is item 1 + This is item 1.1 + This is item 1.2 * This is item 2 * This is item 2.1 * This is item 2.2 ``` **Output:** * This is item 1 + This is item 1.1 + This is item 1.2 * This is item 2 * This is item 2.1 * This is item 2.2 --- ### 9. Numbered list **Code:** ```markdown 1. This is numbered list 2. This is the second list 1. This is a sub-item 2. This is another sub-item ``` **Output:** 1. This is numbered list 2. This is the second list 1. This is a sub-item 2. This is another sub-item --- ### 10. Tables **Code:** ```markdown | Tables | Are | Cool | |----------|:-------------:|------:| | col 1 is | left-aligned | $2x+1$ | | col 2 is | centered | 12 | | col 3 is | right-aligned | Hello | ``` **Output:** | Tables | Are | Cool | |----------|:-------------:|------:| | col 1 is | left-aligned | $2x+1$ | | col 2 is | centered | 12 | | col 3 is | right-aligned | Hello | --- ### 11. R Plot output **Code Chunk:** ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} normal <- rnorm(1000, mean=1, sd=1) par(mfrow = c(1, 2)) hist(normal, main = "HISTOGRAM") plot(density(normal), col = 'red', lwd = 2, main = "DENSITY") ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](index_files/figure-html/unnamed-chunk-2-1.png){width=672} ::: ::: **Code Chunk (with ggplot2):** ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} # https://ggplot2.tidyverse.org/ # install.packages("ggplot2") library(ggplot2) e <- ggplot(mpg, aes(cty, hwy, colour = class)) e + geom_point(aes(colour = factor(manufacturer))) ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](index_files/figure-html/unnamed-chunk-3-1.png){width=672} ::: ::: --- ## True Dynamic Documents in R Now for the most important part! Let's make a truly dynamic document with citation, footnotes^[You can write footnote here] and a bibliography! This is the dynamic document in R developed by @R-core.^[For minimum requirements for referencing see citations.bib file] **Code Chunk:** ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} # Create a sample data file if it doesn't exist if(!file.exists("scorer2014.csv")) { scorer_data <- data.frame( name = c("Rodriguez", "Muller", "Neymer", "Messi"), value = c(10, 15, 8, 12) ) write.csv(scorer_data, "scorer2014.csv", row.names = FALSE) } scorer <- read.csv("scorer2014.csv", header = TRUE) barplot(scorer$value, names.arg = scorer$name, main = "Scorer Values", col = "lightblue") ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](index_files/figure-html/unnamed-chunk-4-1.png){width=672} ::: ::: What makes the document dynamic is that the output above will change as input file (data) changes. To see this, let's generate 5 random numbers and get their sum. And see how this changes as a text! **Code Chunk:** ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} ## Pick 5 random numbers/integers from 0 to 10 set.seed(NULL) # Ensure true randomness each time random.int <- sample(0:10, size = 5, replace = TRUE) random.int ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` [1] 9 1 10 2 10 ``` ::: ::: Try ``` The sum of your 5 random numbers is 'r sum(random.int)'. ``` For example, in this case, we get the following output: The sum of your 5 random numbers is **32**. Run this several times and you will get different sums as you pick different numbers! **AMAZING!** ## Footnotes, Citation, and References Adding a footnote is easy using hat ^ with contents inside square brackets like this.`^[This is a footnote]` Referencing and citations are a little tricky. You need two things: 1. Create s separate file which contains all your references in BibTex form, call it, say `references.bib` and place it in the same folder as your document file. 2. In the **yaml** at the top of your document file include the line `bibliography: references.bib`. This links your document with the references.bib file. Here is an exampe of a BibTex which you can include in your references.bib ```bibtex @article{YoonMudida2020, author = {Yoon, Yong and Mudida, Robert}, title = {Social and Economic Transformation in Tanzania and South Korea: Ujamaa and Saemaul Undong in the 1970s Compared}, journal = {Seoul Journal of Economics}, volume = {33}, number = {2}, pages = {195--231}, year = {2020}, publisher = {Institute of Economic Research, Seoul National University}, issn = {1225-0279}, url = {https://hdl.handle.net/10371/168254} } ``` And to cite this, just place `@YoonMudida2020` in the text. As an added bonus, the full reference will appear at the end of the document!
